name: fix_sh_word_splitting_find
description: Fixes for-loop-over-find word splitting that mangles spaced filenames
prompts: archive_old.sh moves stale files into an archive subdirectory, but `for f in $(find ...)` word-splits the results - a file named 'annual report.txt' becomes two bogus tokens and the mv fails. Fix archive_old.sh (POSIX sh) so filenames with spaces work: `find ... -exec` or a `find | while IFS= read -r` loop are both fine. Keep the behavior: only regular files directly in <dir> older than <days> days move to <dir>/archive/, one 'archived: <basename>' line each, exit 0.

setup_files.archive_old.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# archive_old.sh <dir> <days>: move files not modified in <days> days
# into <dir>/archive/. BUG: the for-loop over $(find ...) word-splits on
# spaces, mangling filenames like "annual report.txt".

dir=$1
days=$2
mkdir -p "$dir/archive"

for f in $(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -mtime +"$days"); do
    mv "$f" "$dir/archive/"
    echo "archived: $(basename "$f")"
done

test_setup_files.test_archive.py:
import os, subprocess, time

os.makedirs('data', exist_ok=True)
old = time.time() - 10 * 86400
for name in ['annual report.txt', 'plain.txt']:
    with open(f'data/{name}', 'w') as f:
        f.write(name)
    os.utime(f'data/{name}', (old, old))
with open('data/fresh.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('new')

r = subprocess.run(['sh', 'archive_old.sh', 'data', '5'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
assert r.returncode == 0, f'exit {r.returncode}: {r.stderr}'

archived = sorted(os.listdir('data/archive'))
assert archived == ['annual report.txt', 'plain.txt'], f'archive contents: {archived}'
assert sorted(os.listdir('data')) == ['archive', 'fresh.txt'], sorted(os.listdir('data'))
assert 'archived: annual report.txt' in r.stdout, f'stdout: {r.stdout!r}'
print('PASS')

reference_solution.archive_old.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# archive_old.sh <dir> <days>: move files not modified in <days> days
# into <dir>/archive/.

dir=$1
days=$2
mkdir -p "$dir/archive"

find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -mtime +"$days" | while IFS= read -r f; do
    mv "$f" "$dir/archive/"
    echo "archived: $(basename "$f")"
done
exit 0
